messages:
oliver: FYI we're publishing a breaking-but-necessary change to the Python SDK docs + a deprecation timeline for the legacy logging hooks. Full migration guide is up in the docs repo and staged. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/722

jazmin: TL;DR for customers?

oliver: Short: redwood-sdk v2.0 changes the logging hook API and tightens the default model-validation behavior. Old logging hooks (`client.on_log`) are deprecated and replaced with a structured logger interface (`client.logger.bind(...)`). We also tightened the payload validation for generate() so some loosely-typed inputs that used to succeed will now raise ValidationError. Migration guide shows examples.

kevin: Any timeline or compatibility window?

oliver: Yes 30-day deprecation window for logging hooks (warnings start today), compatibility shim available for 30 days that emits a WARN on first import. Payload validation: it's a hard change in v2.0; however we published a compatibility flag `client.config.compat.strict_validation=false` to preserve old behavior for 45 days while teams update prompts/input shapes. Recommend upgrading code by 2026-07-15.

jazmin: Can you paste the small migration snippet for the logger? Might be useful for the KB and quick reference.

oliver: Sure: 
```
# old (deprecated)
client.on_log(lambda record: print(record['message']))

# new (structured logger)
from structlog import get_logger
logger = get_logger("redwood")
client.logger = logger
client.logger.info("generation.start", prompt_id=pid)
```

kevin: Where are we documenting the ValidationError schema? Support will need examples of the common mismatches.

oliver: Added a "Validation errors and fixes" appendix in the migration guide with 6 common cases (missing fields, nested lists vs strings, numeric types, embedding size mismatches). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/722/files. I'll tag @support for review.

jazmin: Release note copy for customers? Keep it short.

oliver: Draft blurb: "redwood-sdk v2.0 introduces a structured logger API and stricter input validation to improve observability and model safety. Please follow the 1-minute migration checklist in the docs; a compatibility flag is available for a short window." Use that for the changelog and email.

release-bot: release published: redwood-sdk 2.0.0 on PyPI  https://pypi.org/project/redwood-sdk/2.0.0 :tada:

docs-bot: Docs site updated: /sdk/v2/migration guide and validation appendix deployed to staging. CDN invalidation scheduled for 09:15 UTC.

kevin: Action items: @jazmin write the one-minute migration checklist and customer email; @support review the validation appendix and draft canned replies; @oliver add a short note in the Console release banner. We'll monitor errors via the docs analytics and support queue for 2 weeks.

ojazmin: Got it - I'll post the checklist in community and pin it. Also scheduling a 20-min office hours tomorrow to walk through the migration examples.

oliver: Thanks all. Quick reminder: for downstream repos/examples, please remove `client.on_log` usages and prefer structured logger examples. If anyone needs the compatibility shim we can extend it case-by-case but prefer direct migration. :rocket:
